en: The Method for Taking Refuge, Recitation, and Offering to the Great Sage Hevajra (the Joyful Double-Body), Maheśvara, and Vināyaka-rāja,
translated by the Tripiṭaka Śramaṇa Śubhakarasiṃha.
The Great Sage Maheśvara is the Heavenly King Maheśvara;
he has Umā as his wife.
He begot three thousand sons; of these,
fifteen hundred were on his left,
with Vināyaka-rāja as the foremost.
He performs various evil deeds and leads one hundred and seven thousand classes of vināyakas;
among his right-hand followers, fifteen hundred śatānīkas have the deity Śubha as their leader.
He cultivates all manner of virtuous benefits and leads a retinue of one hundred and seventy-eight thousand beings who possess various meritorious arts and skillful upholding.
This is the King Śanayaka.
He is an emanation of Avalokiteśvara.
In order to harmonize with the evil conduct of that King Vināyaka, he was born into the same class as him and became his brother and wife;
thus he manifested the form of embracing him in a single body.
The original causes and conditions are fully detailed in the *Mahāvidyāmantra-caura-sūtra*.
Now, for the sake of all practitioners,
I shall briefly explain the sequence of the altar rites, recitation, and offerings.
If one does not understand this teaching,
it will be difficult to achieve accomplishment in other sublime dharmas,
and obstacles will be many.
Therefore, one should first cultivate this path.
If there are virtuous men or women who wish to make offerings to this deity in order to seek merit and welfare, [they should do so].
Carve its image from fragrant wood,
having the husband and wife stand embracing one another;
five inches in height, with an elephant's head and a human body.
He wears celestial garments and a lower robe; the husband sits on the lower part of the lotus stalk and the wife on the upper part.
The four petals serve as their seat.
Once the image has been completed,
its price must not be exchanged.
It should not be placed in a private room, but kept in a Buddha hall.
The mantra of the Great Body is as follows:

*Namaḥ vinayukeśāya* (1) *haṣṭimoghasa* (2) *tadyathā* (3) *oṃ dhaye ha dhaye ha* (4) *vinayuka ha* (5) *vinayuka ha* (6) *dharayuka ha* (7) *paridharayuka ha* (8) *saṅgakṛti* (9) *saṅgakṛta* (10) *sañcigarā* (11) *svāhā* (12). This mantra of the Great Body is used for the rites of pacifying calamities (*śāntika*) and for endearing (*vaśīkaraṇa*).
The mantra recited in the heart is:
Oṃ kīli kīlaya. This mantra is for the method of increasing the accumulation of merit.
The Heart-to-Heart mantra (Cittacitta-mantra) is as follows:
Oṃ kṣe kṣe hūṃ phaṭ. This mantra is used for the method of subduing and taming enemies.
Regarding the bodily mudrā: with both hands, interlace the little fingers and ring fingers inwardly.
The two middle fingers and the two index fingers are interlaced and held upright;
the two thumbs are held side by side and straight upward.
This is called the Fundamental Mudrā.
Seal the heart, forehead, throat, and crown of the head with this mudrā to accomplish the rite of protecting the body.
For the mantra and mudrā at the heart: grasp the right ring finger and little finger.
Place the middle finger and index finger together, overlapping and vertical;
the thumbs are both held straight up. This is a subsidiary mudrā of the aforementioned body mudrā.
With this mudrā, protect the pure offerings as well as the bathing water and oil.
The Heart-of-the-Heart Mantra Seal: Form the vajra-bond with both hands and place the palms together at the forehead.
Recite the mantra and cast it toward evil persons, enemies, thieves, and the like.
It must certainly be subdued.
The Ritual for the First Altar: Construct a circular altar measuring two cubits in diameter, made by smearing it with a mixture of *gomaya* and yellow earth.
And one prepares the two types of offerings, namely:
*argha* water, unguents, seasonal flowers, burning incense, *guggulu*, *turushka*, *mūlaka*, and round pills;
as well as pure clarified butter and honey.
Seasonal fruits, confections,
milk-rice porridge, and various delicacies—
each type of offering was prepared in duplicate.
Place [the items] to the left and right of the altar.
Separately, store one *sheng* of pure sesame oil in a bronze cauldron.
Recite the Great Body Dharani (*Mahākāya-dhāraṇī*) one hundred and eight times to protect and purify it.
Thereafter, warm the oil and bathe the honored image.
The mantra for consecrating the water is as follows:

Oṃ anābhāśari bale naha (recite seven times) to perform the ritual bathing. Second, the method for recitation and offering: The Mother’s Heart Seal—bind the two hands internally with the thumbs against each other.
Place both thumbs side by side, each touching the index finger.
The mantra is:
Oṃ śanairga svāhā. Recite this three times. Next is the heart mudrā of Padmāmbā, which is the same as that of the Mother [Buddha] described previously.
Simply extend the right index finger and move it back and forth.
The mantra is:
Oṃ aruliga svāhā. Recite this three times. Next is the Heart Mudrā of Vajrayoginī; the mudrā is the same as the previous one.
Move the left index finger back and forth.
Recite the mantra:
Oṃ vajra-dhṛtika svāhā, three times. Next, perform the Armor Seal (*kavaca-mudrā*): clench the left hand into a fist and place it against the waist.
Form the same fist-mudrā with the right hand and place it upon five locations:
the forehead, the left and right shoulders, the heart, and the throat.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ kuru kuru phaṭ hūṃ. Next, for the mudrā and mantra of the consecrated cleansing water, use the Vajra mudrā and recite:
Oṃ kili kili vajra hūṃ phaṭ seven times. Then, using the fragmentary root mudrā, protect the ritual implements within the consecrated maṇḍala and recite the Great Body Mantra three times.
Next, prostrate before the honored image and repent;
then, rejoice and entreat [the Buddhas].
Next, give rise to mindfulness and contemplation.
This venerable Lord Īśvara is none other than the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana;
for the benefit of sentient beings who lack merit, he has manifested in this form.
This image is manifested through skillful transformation;
those who give rise to this thought of contemplation, take refuge,
and make offerings will certainly attain an immeasurable accumulation of merit.
Next, bind the boundary of the earth: touch the ground with the root mudrā and recite the heart mantra three times to summon it.
Next, for the boundaries of the four directions, use the aforementioned mudrā and mantra as appropriate.
The four boundaries are thus established all around.
Next, one should protect the pure land with the seal-mantra for transforming the pure land;
these seven locations are to be seen at the end [of the ritual].
Next, for the mudrā of the chariot and carriage:
with the two hands joined at the palms, open the palms;
extend both index fingers straight upward, with their tips touching one another.
Using the two thumbs to strike the tips of the two middle fingers, recite the mantra:
Oṃ tūru tūru hūṃ, three times. Next, for the invocation mudrā: it is the same as the fundamental seal described previously.
Move only the thumbs back and forth.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vāgīśvaranīpate. Recite this seven times. Next, perform the four-petal sitting: join the two hands in *añjali*.
The two index fingers are placed side by side;
the two ring fingers and the two little fingers are joined together;
and the left and right middle fingers and ring fingers [are likewise joined].
Each petal is joined at its base and opened upright,
thereby forming a four-petaled seat.
Recite the heart-mantra within your mind.
One should then visualize the Noble One coming and sitting upon this seat.
Next, bind the seal and recite the mantra for the space-element (*ākāśadhātu*) as before;
by rotating the mudrā three times upward, it is accomplished.
Next, bind the Fire-Flame Mudrā: secretly cover the back of the right hand with the left hand,
interlace the fingers, and extend both thumbs straight upward,
keeping them about two inches apart.
The mantra is as follows: Oṃ āsaṃmukhi hūṃ.
Recite this three times. Then, with a tranquil mind and clear mindfulness, perform the rite of offering. Join the palms in the vajra-mudrā and recite the mantra.
Recite "Oṃ eṣa svāhā" eighteen times. Next, place the sacred image into a cauldron of warm oil, beginning with the *argha* water;
perform each mudrā in its proper sequence.
Take it up, hold it aloft, prostrate, and make offerings to it.
As for the mudrā: form two fists with both hands and place the offering vessel upon them.
With a mind of careful sincerity, one should perform the offering with mental attention. The *āveśa* mantra is:
Oṃ hūṃ naliñjaye svāhā. [This is followed by] the mudrās for the various offerings such as flowers and incense.
All are identical.
The mantra is:
OṂ HŪṂ NĀRYE SVĀHĀ. Recite this three times for each; offer only wine with the mudrā and mantra, and offer argha water.
Next, perform the Maṇi-offering mudrā: join the two hands in the vajra-clasp;
form the two index fingers like jewels;
by extending the two thumbs, it is accomplished.
The mantra is as follows:
Namo amoghapūjāmaṇipadmaprasādita-tathāgata-vairocanasamantaprabhāsa hūṃ. Reciting this three times, vast offering implements that pervade the entire dharma-realm are instantly accomplished.
Next, chant the praise of the four wisdoms. With vajra palms joined,
place them at the forehead, then move them to the left and right,
circling them as a seal.
Next, recite the mantra of praise for the Noble One three times.
The mudrā is the same as before:
Oṃ gadāpāṇi śānti svasti mahāgadāpāṇi svāhā. Next, perform the fundamental mudrā.
Recite the Great Body Dharani seven times.
Seal the five parts of the body with mudras.
Pay homage to the Tathāgata Mahāvairocana seven times.
Next, perform seven prostrations to the *Gāthā-paṭhita-brahma-jña*.
Then, perform the recitation;
using a ladle, scoop up the oil.
He performed ablutions over the image’s body seven hundred times within a single day;
at dawn, he performed them four hundred times.
Recite this three hundred times at midday.
At the moment of the formal oil consecration,
maintain a sincere and reverent mind, and do not give rise to other thoughts.
At the conclusion of every one hundred and eight recitations,
offer praise and worship;
repeatedly make vows and set forth the matters you have in mind.
If [this is practiced] for three days up to seven days,
all virtuous aspirations will be fulfilled according to one's wishes,
and all evil matters will be completely extinguished.
This is the realm of Īśvara, the Heaven of Making Use of Others' Transformations;
he descended to travel through the lower realms because his body was enveloped by the whirlpools of the wind-circle.
Using substances such as wine, medicinal herbs, radishes, and oil,
and because he constantly observes the fast, he does not accept offerings in the evening;
the food thus offered is consumed by the mantra-reciter himself.
Physical strength, merit, and longevity shall all be increased.
Third, the method for binding the nose and joining [the deity] instantaneously: if one performs the ritual and makes offerings to the Honored One for three days up to seven days.
If there is no response to one's recollections and aspirations,
burn incense once more, make a vow, and explain the reasons for what you intend.
Take white thread and recite the Great Body Dharani one hundred and eight times.
Recite the mantra over a thread of *sūtra* and tie one hundred and eight knots.
Cut it into two parts and tie them to the tips of the nostrils of the two deities.
For the mudrā, use the śaṅkha-mudrā.
Form the two hands into the vajra-añjali mudrā by interlacing the index fingers and thumbs of both hands respectively;
this is formed after binding [the thumbs] at the nose.
For three days and nights, one must not travel elsewhere nor converse with others.
Fourth, the Method of Harmonization: the head of that elephant is human, yet it is afflicted by a sore.
He has six protruding tusks;
his nose is like a thread;
and in his left hand, he grasps a sword.
Next, the left hand holds a fruit platter;
the lower right hand holds a wheel;
and the upper right hand holds a staff.
Next, hold the cord with the hand;
lower the hand to grasp the fangs.
When there is a state of wrath, [perform this].
In front of this image, construct a small circular mandala.
Arrange offerings of food, drink, wine, medicine, radishes, *modaka* cakes, and so forth, and perform the invitation ritual.
Join the two palms together and bend the two index fingers.
Grasp the tip of the thumb.
Recite the mantra:
*Hūṃ hūṃ chaduluparāmadatnaye svāhā*. Seven times. At each repetition, move the index finger back and forth.
Then, with a heart of utmost sincerity, one should prostrate and repent;
offer each of the ritual implements while praising them,
and recite the mantra of Maheśvara one thousand and eight times.
As for the mudrā:
interlace the two little fingers and the two ring fingers within the palms;
extend the two middle fingers so that their tips touch one another.
Place both index fingers upon the first joints of the backs of the middle fingers.
The mantra is:
Oṃ vidara-saṃni-pralamba-rātra-ni-jita ni-jita vidani vidani svāhā. Having completed the offering, state the matter you have in mind.
Retrieve the ritual implements from within the mandala during the first watch of the night.
Outside, construct a water mandala;
with those offerings and others, mix them with clear water and sprinkle them upon the water mandala.
And sprinkle [the water] in all directions.
The mantra is:
*āveśaya ghasa pṛccha*. This is the fifth method for accomplishing all activities. If one seeks to win the affection of a husband (*bhartṛ*) or others, [one should proceed as follows].
Burn *pulaka* incense for three days and nights;
establish an altar and perform offerings while reciting the *Bhagavān-mantra*.
Three times each day, perform the mudrā one thousand times per session.
For the mudrā:
join the left and right little fingers and ring fingers together.
Interlace the fingers so they enter within the palms.
The two middle fingers are held straight upright with their tips joined; when opened, they must not touch.
The two thumbs press down upon the ring fingers.
Seal the seven locations:
namely, the two shoulders, below the throat, between the eyebrows, at the hairline, on the crown of the head, and at the back of the head.
The mantra is as follows:
Oṃ vinayugaśānanāthadevagaruṇāya svāhā. If one wishes to subjugate an evil person, write that person's name beneath one's own feet.
For one day and night, he abstains from food and drink,
forms the *abhiṣeka-mudrā*,
and recites the *abhicāra* mantra.
At that time, recite separately one thousand times.
As for the mudrā: join the two hands in *añjali* and press them downward.
Extend the two middle fingers straight upward with their tips joined together.
Bend the two middle fingers and extend the two index and two little fingers so that their tips touch one another;
then press the two thumbs down upon the backs of the two middle fingers.
Bend each of the two index fingers over the thumb;
let the tips of the thumbs and the tips of the index fingers move against one another.
Recite: *Oṃ gaṇapati abighoruṣa svāhā*.
If one wishes to cease idle speech,
take well-water from the morning blossoms and recite the Great Body Dharani one hundred times.
Sprinkle enchanted water toward that direction,
and the [hostile] speech will surely cease.
For all matters one seeks and contemplates:
One should practice and recite these three mantras—the Body Mantra, the Heart Mantra, and so forth—as one pleases.
There is no worldly undertaking that will not be accomplished; this is the essential path of worldly dharmas.
As for the secret arts of human relations and the sudden dharma of non-attainment—could there be anything that surpasses this?
I now seek out the profound treasury of the secret teachings to transmit them to the final age;
may those of wise mind who possess aspiration take heed.
It is fitting that you test this and be cautious; do not transmit it recklessly.
Recorded by the śramaṇa Kuaidao, residing at Fēngshān.
